findings.title: Deadline misses: ctrl missed 39 of 98 jobs (period 20 ms, worst release-to-completion 141 ms)
findings.root_cause: Task ctrl has a 20 ms period (from its pf_period markers) but 39 of 98 jobs finished more than one period after their release, worst 141 ms (job 71 started 138 ms late, events #14313, #14314). The misses overlap F2 (CPU starvation), which is the cause.
findings.fix: Fix the upstream cause first (see the linked finding). If the job legitimately needs more time, raise the period or shorten the work.

findings.title: CPU starvation: ctrl (prio 20) kept off the CPU up to 140 ms by hog (prio 40), 5 times
findings.root_cause: ctrl (priority 20) was ready to run but waited up to 140 ms because hog (priority 40) kept the CPU, 5 times. With fixed-priority scheduling this is expected whenever a higher-priority thread is busy; it is a problem only if ctrl has a deadline.
findings.fix: Bound the high-priority thread's CPU burst (sleep/yield or move work to a lower priority), use sporadic scheduling (SCHED_SPORADIC), or adaptive partitioning to guarantee a CPU budget.
